headline: Suspends the federal debt limit until January 2025, caps federal spending for two years, restarts student loan payments, and changes SNAP and TANF work rules.
what_it_does: This law lets the federal government keep borrowing by suspending the debt limit through January 1, 2025. It sets spending limits for most yearly federal programs in fiscal years 2024 and 2025 and takes back some unspent money, including leftover COVID-19 funds and some IRS funding from the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act. It ends the pause on federal student loan payments and interest and changes work rules for SNAP (food stamps) and TANF (cash aid). It also changes how federal agencies do environmental reviews for projects and approves permits for the Mountain Valley Pipeline.

who_it_affects.how: The pause on payments, the 0% interest rate, and forced collections ended 60 days after June 30, 2023, and the Education Department cannot extend the pause without Congress's approval.

who_it_affects.group: SNAP recipients ages 50 to 54 who are able to work and have no dependents
who_it_affects.how: Work requirements that used to apply only up to age 49 were extended step by step to people up to age 54 by fiscal year 2025, ending in 2030.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans, people experiencing homelessness, and former foster youth age 24 or younger who receive SNAP
who_it_affects.how: They are now exempt from the extra SNAP work requirements for adults without dependents, through 2030.

who_it_affects.group: States that run SNAP and TANF
who_it_affects.how: States can grant fewer SNAP work-requirement exemptions (8% instead of 12%), face tighter TANF work-rate calculations, and must report job and earnings results for people who leave TANF.
States face stricter rules on meeting work participation rates, which may change how they run work programs for these families.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies and programs funded by yearly spending bills
who_it_affects.how: Spending is capped for fiscal years 2024 and 2025, with automatic cuts if the limits are exceeded, and unspent money in many programs is taken back.

who_it_affects.group: Companies and groups building projects that need federal approval
who_it_affects.how: Environmental reviews now have page limits, deadlines, and a single lead agency, and project sponsors can go to court if an agency misses a deadline.

who_it_affects.group: People and groups challenging the Mountain Valley Pipeline in Virginia and West Virginia
who_it_affects.how: All permits for the pipeline are approved by law and cannot be challenged in court, including lawsuits already pending.
Some unspent funding it received from the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act is taken back.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted June 3, 2023. Student loan pause ended 60 days after June 30, 2023; SNAP age changes began 90 days after enactment; spending caps apply to fiscal years 2024 and 2025; debt limit suspended through January 1, 2025; most TANF changes start October 1, 2024, with some on October 1, 2025.
